title: TCP three-way handshake
body: TCP establishes a reliable connection using a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK, before either side sends application data.

title: B-tree indexes
body: Most relational databases use B-tree indexes by default because they keep lookup, insert, and range-scan costs logarithmic in the number of rows.

title: CAP theorem
body: The CAP theorem states that a distributed data store can provide at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at the same time.

title: Garbage collection generations
body: Generational garbage collectors separate young and old objects because most objects die young, so scanning the young generation frequently is cheap and effective.

title: HTTP idempotency
body: GET, PUT, and DELETE are defined as idempotent HTTP methods, meaning repeating the same request produces the same result on the server.

title: Consistent hashing
body: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping when nodes are added or removed from a distributed cache, unlike simple modulo hashing.

title: Write-ahead logging
body: Write-ahead logging requires that changes be recorded in a durable log before they are applied to the actual data pages, enabling crash recovery.

title: Vector embeddings
body: A vector embedding maps text, images, or other data into a fixed-length numeric vector such that semantically similar inputs end up close together in the vector space.

title: Cosine similarity
body: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors rather than their magnitude, which makes it a common choice for comparing text embeddings.

title: Read replicas
body: Read replicas offload read traffic from a primary database by asynchronously copying committed writes, at the cost of eventual rather than immediate consistency.

title: Idempotency keys
body: An idempotency key lets a client safely retry a non-idempotent request, such as a payment, without risking the operation being applied twice.

title: Bloom filters
body: A Bloom filter is a space-efficient probabilistic structure that can definitively say an item is not in a set, but can only say an item is probably in it.

title: Least privilege
body: The principle of least privilege grants a user or service only the permissions strictly required for its task, reducing the blast radius of a compromised credential.

title: Rate limiting algorithms
body: Token bucket and leaky bucket are two common rate-limiting algorithms; token bucket allows short bursts while leaky bucket enforces a strictly smooth output rate.

title: Circuit breakers
body: A circuit breaker stops calling a failing downstream service for a cooldown period, preventing cascading failures across a distributed system.

title: Sharding
body: Sharding splits a large dataset across multiple database instances by a partition key, trading cross-shard query complexity for horizontal scalability.

title: Optimistic concurrency control
body: Optimistic concurrency control lets transactions proceed without locking and only checks for conflicts at commit time, which works well when contention is rare.

title: IAM roles vs users
body: An IAM role is an identity with permissions that can be assumed temporarily by a trusted principal, avoiding the need to distribute long-lived access keys.

title: Content-addressed storage
body: Content-addressed storage names an object by the cryptographic hash of its contents, so identical data is automatically deduplicated and any corruption is detectable.

title: Semantic search
body: Semantic search retrieves results based on meaning rather than exact keyword overlap, typically by comparing vector embeddings with a distance metric like cosine or Euclidean.

title: Idempotent infrastructure
body: Infrastructure-as-code tools aim to be idempotent: applying the same configuration twice should converge to the same end state rather than duplicating resources.

title: Backpressure
body: Backpressure is a mechanism where a slow consumer signals an upstream producer to slow down, preventing unbounded queue growth and memory exhaustion.

title: Multi-tenant isolation
body: Multi-tenant systems isolate tenants either physically, with separate databases per tenant, or logically, with a shared schema and a tenant-id column enforced on every query.

title: Blue-green deployment
body: Blue-green deployment runs two identical production environments and switches traffic between them, allowing near-instant rollback if the new version misbehaves.

title: Retry with jitter
body: Adding random jitter to exponential backoff retries prevents many clients from retrying in synchronized waves that overwhelm a recovering service.

title: Zero-downtime schema migration
body: A zero-downtime schema migration typically adds a new column as nullable, backfills it in batches, then makes it required only after all writers are updated.

title: Query planner statistics
body: A relational database's query planner relies on table statistics, such as row counts and value distributions, to choose between a sequential scan and an index scan.

title: Event sourcing
body: Event sourcing stores every state change as an immutable event rather than overwriting a row, letting the current state be rebuilt by replaying the event log.

title: Approximate nearest neighbor search
body: Approximate nearest neighbor algorithms like HNSW trade a small amount of recall for large speedups when searching millions of high-dimensional vectors.

title: Secrets rotation
body: Automated secrets rotation periodically replaces credentials such as database passwords or API keys, limiting how long a leaked credential remains useful to an attacker.
